diagnosis.summary: Request rates across all four services have risen sharply above their baselines, with product-service at 26.85 rps versus 14.98, cart-service at 6.3 rps versus 2.05, order-service at 8.07 rps versus 2.97, and payment-service at 3.98 rps versus 0.94. DynamoDB write and read capacity consumption has risen in proportion on cart-service and order-service. No 5xx errors have been observed on any service, and the stack appears to be absorbing the load at this time.
diagnosis.root_cause: A broad traffic surge across all services is the most likely root cause.
evidence: product-service request rate rose from 14.98 to 26.85 rps, an increase of roughly 1.8x.
cart-service request rate rose from 2.05 to 6.30 rps (~3.1x), order-service from 2.97 to 8.07 rps (~2.7x), and payment-service from 0.94 to 3.98 rps (~4.2x).
cart-service DynamoDB write capacity rose from 122.8 to 378 WCU/min (~3.1x) and order-service write capacity rose from 56.6 to 239 WCU/min (~4.2x).
order-service DynamoDB read capacity rose from 60.8 to 122.5 RCU/min, approximately doubling.
order-service p50 latency rose from 3.555 ms to 7.245 ms, roughly doubling.
error_rate_5xx remains at 0 for both product-service and cart-service, indicating no errors at current load.
recommended_actions: Monitor all four services for rising p95 latency or 5xx errors; if they remain near baseline no immediate change is needed.
Watch product-service db_consumed_read_capacity and read_throttle_events closely, as read load on the Products table grows with request rate and could approach provisioned limits.
Check lambda_throttle_count on all services to confirm the shared Lambda concurrency limit is not being approached.
Determine whether the traffic increase is expected (promotion, launch, or a client retrying) before making capacity changes.
If latency or errors begin to rise, apply rate and burst limits on the API Gateway stage to protect the stack while the traffic source is identified.
